Table-shape lands with a massive win. Stock TabularStore + query_table tool + bench wiring deliver r@1/r@5/r@k = 100% vs Phase 0's 58.3%/66.7%/75% on the same fixture — a +33-41pp lift, in ~1ms. The bench cell (table_sql_oracle) uses fixture-supplied SQL to measure the architectural ceiling; NL→SQL generation is the agent's job at chat time via the production query_table tool, which interpolates registered table schemas into its description so the model has the grounded context without a separate list_tables round-trip. The thesis from the data-retrieval-primitives notes is validated: tabular data needs to be retrieved AS tables.

Context Package + Contract Bundle land as the architectural shift the data-retrieval-primitives spike was building toward. RetrievalContextPackage wraps shape-aware retrieval in one envelope with intent / access (user_id scoping) / proof (per-hit provenance) / budget (token cap). ContractBundle declares per-role what each slot needs from which shaped store; assemble_package walks the contract, dispatches to episodic / tree / tabular, returns a complete or incomplete package. Required-slot misses surface in missing_required_slots so the agent gets told what's missing rather than working with silently-incomplete context. Worked end-to-end demo: retrieval_eval/contracts/returns_handler.yaml + test_contract_returns_handler.py pulls customer history (episodic) + refund policy (episodic) + matching orders (tabular) in one call, against the same synthetic returns CSV Phases 0-2 used. 34 new tests (13 package + 17 contract + 4 end-to-end), 1934/1934 green. Pure module — no model dependency, no I/O beyond the stores it's given. CLI/chat integration intentionally deferred — the primitive is ready for a caller (a tool that materializes a package, a per-role session-start renderer) when there's a use case.

Landed. SlotSpec gained auto_merge: bool = False field, tree-only via __post_init__ validation. When True, the orchestrator fetches max_hits*3 candidates from the tree store, then post-processes via _merge_sibling_clusters: any cluster of 2+ sibling leaves under the same parent collapses to a single hit at the parent path. The eval at atc-retrieval bypasses the contract orchestrator and is unchanged — auto_merge only applies via assemble_package; a follow-up could thread auto_merge into make_tree_search_fn if the user wants the retrieval-only baseline to reflect it too.
